title: Set 274

sentences.ko: 요즘 달걀값 얼마나 하는지 봤어? 예전엔 가격도 안 보고 그냥 한 팩 집었는데, 이젠 그 앞에 서서 가격부터 보고 있어. 그러고는 결국 사. 달리 뭘 먹겠어?
sentences.text: Have you seen how much eggs cost now? I used to just grab a carton without even looking, but now I stand there checking the price, and then I buy them anyway, because what else am I going to eat?

alts.text: Eggs are so expensive now, have you noticed? I used to grab a carton without looking. Now I stand there checking the price, and I still buy them, 'cause what else am I gonna eat?

Have you noticed how expensive eggs have become? I used to purchase a carton without even looking at the price, but now I find myself checking it, and then I buy them regardless, because what else would I eat?

sentences.note: **grab a carton** 은 달걀 한 팩을 별생각 없이 집어 든다는 말이에요. **what else am I going to eat?** 는 다른 방법이 없다는 체념을 담은 되물음이에요.

sentences.ko: 저기, 주문이 잘못 온 것 같아. 이거 엄청 매운맛이라고 적혀 있는데, 난 분명 순한 맛 시켰거든. 네가 먹을 거 아니면 손대기 전에 가게에 전화할게.
sentences.text: Hey, I think they gave us the wrong order. This one says extra spicy, and I'm pretty sure I asked for mild, so unless you want it, I'm going to call them before we eat any of it.

alts.text: Wait, I think this is the wrong order. It says extra spicy, and I'm pretty sure I ordered mild, so unless you want it, I'm gonna call them before we dig in.
I believe we have received the wrong order. This one is labeled extra spicy, and I am fairly certain I requested mild, so unless you would like it, I will call the restaurant before we eat any of it.

sentences.note: **I'm pretty sure** 는 거의 확신할 때 쓰는 말이에요. **unless you want it** 은 네가 원하지 않는 한이라는 뜻으로, 상대에게 먼저 물어보는 배려가 담겨 있어요.
sentences.situation: 배달 시켰는데 엉뚱한 게 와서 얘기하기

sentences.ko: 윗집 남자가 밤마다 가구를 옮기는 게 분명해. 11시쯤 되면 내 침대 바로 위에서 질질 끄는 소리가 나거든. 그 집 문에 쪽지를 붙여 놨는데 일주일이 지나도 그대로라서, 그 사람이 쪽지를 보기나 했는지 모르겠어.
sentences.text: The guy upstairs must be moving furniture around every night, because around eleven I hear this dragging sound right over my bed. I left a note on his door, but it's been a week and nothing's changed, so I don't even know if he saw it.

alts.text: I swear the guy upstairs moves furniture every night. Around eleven there's this dragging sound right over my bed. I left a note on his door, but it's been a week and still nothing, so who knows if he even saw it.

The gentleman who lives upstairs appears to be moving furniture every night, because at around eleven o'clock I hear a dragging sound directly above my bed. I left a note on his door, but a week has passed and nothing has changed, so I am not certain whether he saw it.

sentences.note: **must be moving** 은 틀림없이 ~하고 있을 거라는 추측이에요. **it's been a week** 는 벌써 일주일이 됐다는 뜻으로 시간이 흐른 것을 말할 때 자주 써요.

sentences.ko: 회사를 그만둘지 계속 왔다 갔다 하고 있어. 작년에 다른 데서 제안 왔을 때 나갔으면 이런 일 안 겪고 있을 텐데, 지금 갈 데도 안 정하고 그만두면 더 후회할까 봐 겁나.
sentences.text: I keep going back and forth about quitting. If I'd left last year when I had that other offer, I wouldn't be dealing with any of this, but if I quit now without something lined up, I'm scared I'll regret it even more.

alts.text: I can't decide if I should quit. If I'd taken that other offer last year, I wouldn't be dealing with any of this, but if I quit now with nothing lined up, I'm scared I'll regret it even more.

I continue to go back and forth about resigning. Had I left last year when I received the other offer, I would not be dealing with any of this, but if I resign now without another position secured, I am afraid I will regret it even more.

sentences.note: **go back and forth** 는 마음을 못 정하고 이랬다저랬다 한다는 뜻이에요. **something lined up** 은 다음 일자리처럼 미리 잡아 둔 것을 말해요.

sentences.ko: 앉을 데 찾으려고 카페를 세 군데나 갔는데, 하나같이 노트북 하는 사람들로 꽉 차 있었어. 그래서 결국 차에서 일했는데, 솔직히 나쁘지 않았어. 한 시간 만에 노트북 배터리가 나가기 전까지는.
sentences.text: I went to three different coffee shops looking for somewhere to sit, and every single one was packed with people on laptops. So I ended up working in my car, which honestly wasn't that bad, until my laptop died after an hour.

alts.text: Tried three coffee shops to find a seat, and every one was packed with laptop people. So I just worked in my car, which wasn't that bad, honestly, till my laptop died an hour in.

I visited three different coffee shops in search of a place to sit, and every one of them was full of people working on laptops. I therefore ended up working in my car, which was not too bad, to be honest, until my laptop battery ran out after an hour.

sentences.note: **packed with** 는 ~로 꽉 찼다는 뜻이에요. **ended up** 은 결국 ~하게 됐다는 말이고, **my laptop died** 는 노트북 배터리가 다 됐다는 뜻이에요.

reviewed: 1번 ko: carton 은 보통 12개들이라 '한 판'(30개)과 안 맞아 '한 팩'으로 고치고, '서서 가격을 들여다보고 있어'를 '그 앞에 서서 가격부터 보고 있어'로 자연스럽게 다듬음
2번 casual: 'I got mild' 는 '순한 맛을 받았다'로도 읽혀 헷갈리므로 'I ordered mild' 로 고침
2번 formal: 같이 먹는 사람에게 'Excuse me' 로 말을 거는 것은 어색해서 빼고, 말투만 올림
2번 ko: '아주 맵게라고 적혀 있는데'가 번역투라 '엄청 매운맛이라고 적혀 있는데'로 고침
3번 casual: 'nothing's different' 는 이 자리에서 원어민이 잘 안 쓰는 말이라 'still nothing' 으로 고침
